issues.title: Global characteristic flow is not guaranteed

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is assumed to be continuous with respect to both \( \mathbf{x} \) and \( t \), and its first-order partial derivatives are also continuous.

issues.failure_explanation: The old standing assumptions give a continuously differentiable velocity but do not prevent finite-time escape. In one dimension, A(x,t)=-x^2 has the solution x(t)=x_T/[1+x_T(t-T)]; for sufficiently large terminal x_T it blows up before time 0 when traced backward. The characteristics do not intersect before escape, so the paper's non-intersection qualification does not supply the missing completeness. Thus the all-time evolved domains, hat-Omega, and the extension proposition can be undefined for an admissible old velocity field.
issues.overall_effect: The extension proposition and all later constructions that require characteristic maps for arbitrary pairs of times lack established inputs. Their conclusions may remain valid after separately assuming a complete invertible flow, but the old C1 assumptions do not provide one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standing global-flow hypothesis requiring the velocity to generate a complete C1 diffeomorphic flow for every pair of times in [0,T]. A sufficient source-compatible condition is the existing local C1 regularity together with a global linear-growth bound on A. Make the evolved domains and every affected support, norm, functional, remapping, existence, stability, and uniqueness result conditional on this hypothesis.
issues.why_classification: Finite-time escape occurs for ordinary smooth fields in the advertised C1 class and leaves the entire affected chain without defined inputs. The added hypothesis is a contained repair that preserves the method and conclusions, but it genuinely restricts the velocity-field class rather than merely correcting notation, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: False L^P-norm invariance under compressible flow

failure_location.quote: the domain of integration remains unchanged as \(\mathbb{R}^d\) before and after the change of variables

issues.failure_explanation: The characteristic displacement depends on the initial spatial point through s(τ). Preserving the integration domain R^d therefore does not make the change of variables measure preserving. For A(x,t)=x, the flow Jacobian is e^{t2-t1}, giving an L^P scaling factor e^{-(t2-t1)/P}. The same erroneous unit-Jacobian premise is repeated for moving bounded domains.
issues.overall_effect: Both norm-invariance lemmas are false for compressible flows. The bounded-functional, existence, stability, and uniqueness arguments consequently lack the norm estimate they invoke as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both exact Lp-invariance assertions by the change-of-variables identity containing the determinant of the inverse flow Jacobian. For bounded moving domains and the compactly supported whole-space data used in the proofs, bound that determinant above and below on the compact flow tube to obtain two-sided norm estimates. Propagate the resulting factors through the bounded-functional, existence, stability, and uniqueness arguments, absorbing their products into the stability constant.
issues.why_classification: Compressibility genuinely destroys the claimed exact norm conservation. Repairing the full chain requires a Jacobian or Liouville estimate and corresponding changes to several downstream estimates; however, this is a contained argument, and comparable norm control preserves the existence, stability, and uniqueness guarantees. The limited weakening and nontrivial lemma exceed a minor repair but require no global reconstruction.

issues.title: Bounded-domain functional evaluates outside its domain

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any \(W \in H(G)\), define the functional \(f\) as follows:

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma quantifies over arbitrary W in H(G) but evaluates W at the characteristic image of x. For example, a constant translation can send every x in a bounded G outside G, where W is undefined. Thus f is not even a well-defined functional on H(G), independently of whether the later boundedness estimate is valid.
issues.overall_effect: The bounded-domain version of the auxiliary functional is undefined. The existence theorem's actual invocation uses the whole-space variant, so this domain defect does not by itself defeat that invocation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the characteristic map F from time tp to tp+Δt, explicitly use the canonical zero extension E_G W of W∈L2(G) and define V(x)=(E_G W)(F(x)). A routine change of variables on the bounded set G then gives |f(W)|≤C_G‖𝔘‖L2(G)‖W‖L2(G), so the bounded-domain functional remains a well-defined bounded linear functional on L2(G).
issues.why_classification: The missing extension makes the printed functional genuinely undefined and is not a uniquely forced transcription correction. Nevertheless, an extension convention already used elsewhere in the source plus a routine local estimate repairs the entire lemma without weakening its substantive bounded-linearity claim, and there are no recorded dependents.

issues.title: Support equality is incompatible with the stated H0 space

failure_location.quote: Since \(\operatorname{supp}\{U^n_i\} = \Omega_i\), it further follows that \(U^n_i \in H_0(\Omega_i)\).

issues.failure_explanation: The L2 calculation establishes only that U_i^n is square integrable. Literal equality supp(U_i^n)=Ω_i does not satisfy the paper's defining condition supp(U_i^n) compactly contained in Ω_i, so the final H0 conclusion does not follow. The same unsupported inference is used for remapped functions and later compact-support arguments.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's H0 conclusion and later uses of elementwise compact support are unsupported under the printed equality convention.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the closed zero-extension space H₀(D):={f∈L2(Rd):f=0 almost everywhere outside D}, which is isometric to L2(D), and state essential-support containment in the closure of D rather than strict compact containment or support equality. Apply this convention consistently to the element functions, remapped functions, test functions, and assembled solution; the restriction, remapping, existence, stability, and uniqueness arguments then retain their existing architecture.
issues.why_classification: The printed inference from support equality to strict compact containment is mathematically false, so this is not a typo. The source's repeated zero-extension construction supports a routine correction of the function-space convention, after which the same L2 scheme and theorem guarantees survive without a new lemma, proof architecture, or meaningful loss.

issues.title: Lost element index in the existence construction
issues.failure_explanation: The Riesz construction must represent, for each Ω_K, the functional integrating U-tilde_K against ψ_K over the corresponding upstream region. As printed, the proof asserts global support for an unindexed ψ and concludes with an integral over the global upstream domain, which is not the local identity required by the discrete scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The printed induction does not connect its first-step representative to the elementwise equation required by the scheme, although the intended local construction is evident.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the element index throughout the first Riesz step: use ψ⁰_K, its upstream region Ω̃¹,⁰_K, the local datum Ũ⁰_K, and the integral over Ω̃¹,⁰_K, and retain the same indexed identity in the induction step.
issues.why_classification: The local target displayed at the start of the proof and the already indexed functional uniquely force these substitutions. Restoring the dropped index changes no inference or construction and directly yields the required elementwise scheme identity, so the defect is transcriptional.

issues.title: Wrong integration variable in the y-split construction
issues.failure_explanation: The quantity J^{ys}_{g,l} supplies the entries of the y-direction right-hand-side matrix. With x fixed, integrating its y-dependent integrand over I_r^{x,*} using dx neither represents the preceding y-invariant nor computes the required matrix entry. Consequently the printed y-update cannot be executed as specified.
issues.overall_effect: The x-direction construction remains usable, but the printed y-direction coefficient update has an invalid right-hand-side definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the definition by J^{ys}_{g,l}(d)=∫_{I^{y,star}_s}U((Gg)^x_r,y,t^y_d)ψ^y(y,t^y_d;φ_l)dy, and use these entries in the stated y-direction right-hand-side matrix and coefficient update.
issues.why_classification: The immediately preceding y-direction invariant fixes x, integrates over the upstream y-cell, and uses dy, so the correction is uniquely forced by the old source. No mathematical argument or algorithmic redesign is needed beyond correcting the copied integration domain and differential.
